bull.b: Gross margin reached 81.3% in Q2, up from 73.5% a year earlier, and management guides 81%–83% for Q3 with an approximately 85% long-term target. This supports a scalable software model and gives future revenue growth greater earnings potential.

SafePath Connect and SDKs/APIs broaden distribution beyond complex carrier integrations, while app-store delivery lowers partner deployment friction. This can expand the addressable partner base and diversify growth opportunities if adoption converts.

Two consecutive quarters of sequential growth, planned customer launches, and a Tier-1 contract extension provide identifiable growth drivers. Successful execution could improve platform utilization and restore scale, although conversion and timing remain important.

bear.b: Revenue fell from $58.4M in 2021 to $16.9M TTM, while Q2 and YTD 2026 also declined year over year. The prolonged contraction indicates weaker scale and makes sustained growth dependent on converting launches and rebuilding demand.

bear.t: Severe cash burn and limited liquidity
bear.b: Operating and free cash flow were both negative $9.0M TTM, while cash was only $2.8M at June 30. This leaves limited self-funded runway, increasing dependence on financing or customer receipts and constraining investment flexibility.

Dependence on large carrier relationships and deployment schedules creates structural concentration risk. A small number of customer decisions can materially affect revenue scale, while competition could reduce pricing power or lower the probability of winning contracts.
